overview: After 1.g3 h5 Black pushes the h-pawn at once, weakening g5 and the kingside without developing. White simply develops with Bg2, Nf3, d4 and can castle on either side, gaining a free hand in the centre. I do not recognise this as a studied line, so these notes come from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Develop normally with Bg2, Nf3, d4 and c4
Exploit the weakened g5 square and the slow h-pawn push
Take the centre while Black has spent a tempo

black_ideas.idea: Hope for a kingside pawn storm with ...h4
Use the h-file if the rook gets there after ...h4xg3

typical_structures.structure: Flank fianchetto set-up with White centre and an advanced Black h-pawn

character.notes: Eccentric, not forcing; White just develops.

soundness.notes: The h-pawn push loses a tempo and weakens the kingside without a concrete gain, so close to dubious for Black.

approach.notes: A joke or simul trick; strong players do not choose 1...h5.

level.notes: Easy to play against, but it is not a repertoire choice.

character.reason: Quiet development for White; Black's idea is slow.

soundness.reason: 1...h5 loses a tempo and weakens g5 for no compensation.

approach.reason: A joke move that strong players do not play.

level.reason: Not a good first repertoire choice and dubious, so never beginner.
